meta.note: Every capability in this physical-intelligence stack has two dates: the year it first worked, and the year it arrived in volume. The distance between them is the lag.

definitions.invented: The year the capability was first demonstrated in a lab, patent, or working prototype.
definitions.shipped: The year it reached high-volume industrial deployment or commercial series production.
definitions.lag: shipped − invented. Where an entry has not shipped, it has no lag.

confidence.label: Dated
confidence.note: Both years are documented and verified in technical literature.

confidence.label: Contested
confidence.note: One date is an editorial judgement call depending on volume thresholds.

confidence.label: Not shipped
confidence.note: Early lab prototype or pilot testing; volume production date unconfirmed.

waitedFor.label: The science
waitedFor.note: Kinematics, dynamics, contact mechanics, or control math was incomplete.

waitedFor.label: A machine
waitedFor.note: Machine tools, sub-micron grinding, or semiconductor lithography were missing.

waitedFor.label: A better reason
waitedFor.note: Incumbent manual labor or hydraulic machinery was dramatically cheaper.

waitedFor.label: Something to run on
waitedFor.note: Required GPU compute, fleet scale, or massive demonstration datasets.

waitedFor.label: Someone to want it
waitedFor.note: Technology worked, but broad industrial demand took decades to develop.

events.label: The industrial robot arm (Unimate)
events.note: George Devol patented programmed article transfer in 1954; Joseph Engelberger commercialized Unimate at GM Trenton die-casting in 1961.

events.label: Strain-wave gearing (Harmonic Drive)
events.note: C. Walton Musser invented strain-wave gearing in 1955. Aerospace and industrial robot joints adopted it for zero-backlash high-ratio reduction.

events.label: RV cycloidal speed reducer
events.note: Lorenz Braren patented the cycloidal principle in 1926. Nabtesco mastered sub-micron pin-wheel grinding in 1985, anchoring heavy robot base joints.

events.label: Sintered NdFeB permanent magnets
events.note: Masato Sagawa (Sumitomo) and John Croat (General Motors) developed Nd₂Fe₁₄B in 1982, quadrupling brushless motor torque density by 1989.

source.what: IEEE Milestone in Nd-Fe-B Permanent Magnets

events.label: Field-Oriented Vector Control (FOC)
events.note: Felix Blaschke (Siemens) formulated vector control in 1971. Required fast digital signal processors (DSPs) before shipping in volume motor drives.

events.label: Deterministic EtherCAT fieldbus
events.note: Beckhoff Automation introduced EtherCAT in 2003. Delivered 100 Mbps sub-microsecond jitter synchronization across 100+ joint axes.

events.label: Robot Operating System (ROS / ROS 2)
events.note: Willow Garage created ROS in 2007. ROS 2 with DDS real-time middleware achieved enterprise production status by 2018.

events.label: Lightweight collaborative robot (UR5)
events.note: Universal Robots developed the UR5 cobot in 2005, introducing modular joints, direct-teaching, and current-based collision detection.

events.label: Proprioceptive Quasi-Direct Drive (QDD)
events.note: Sangbae Kim and Ben Katz pioneered low-inertia QDD actuators at MIT, eliminating gear shock fragility in quadruped and humanoid robots.

events.label: GelSight elastomeric tactile skin
events.note: Edward Adelson invented GelSight at MIT in 2009. Miniaturized camera-based elastomer sensors reached volume series production by 2021.

events.label: MuJoCo contact physics engine
events.note: Emo Todorov published MuJoCo in 2012. Acquired by DeepMind and open-sourced, becoming the standard contact simulator for robot RL.

source.what: MuJoCo: A framework for robot dynamics

events.label: GPU-parallel physics & domain randomization
events.note: NVIDIA Isaac Gym moved thousands of simulation environments onto tensor GPU cores, reducing months of robot RL training to minutes.

source.what: Isaac Gym: High Performance GPU-Based Physics Simulation

events.label: Diffusion Policy for robotic manipulation
events.note: Cheng Chi et al. applied score-based diffusion models to generate multimodal robotic action trajectories from visual observations.

source.what: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Generation via Diffusion

events.label: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models
events.note: Open X-Embodiment, RT-2, and Physical Intelligence π0 combined multimodal web knowledge with robot token actions for zero-shot generalization.

source.what: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X

events.label: Whole-Body Dynamic Control & Locomotion
events.note: Pierre-Brice Wieber and Scott Kuindersma developed quadratic programming whole-body control, enabling Atlas to parkour in 2020.

events.label: Time-of-flight safety laser scanner
events.note: SICK AG introduced certified pulsed laser scanners, dynamically adjusting safety stopping zones as mobile robots navigate human workcells.
